gate_v.note: the runs on a fresh clone of the benchmark, on a commit whose task folder differs from this one only in tests/review/, tests/NOTICE.md and the revision line of environment/assets.sha256: the review files and the notice are read neither by the agent nor by the build of the image nor by the grader, and that commit's asset list named an earlier revision of the asset dataset; its image was built with a local mirror of the same 101 asset files, each with the sha256 the list gives

note: evidence of completability and fairness of this task as this folder holds it (tests/review/README.md); task files relative to the task folder; each entry of `reports` gives the numbers of one body of evidence and the task files it was computed on. `task_files` pins the sha256 of 34 of those files (in the published form also the files of the `publication` entry), and check_index.py recomputes exactly these; the payload of the agent's home is named by the digest of the build tree it was assembled in (`payload_tree_digest`), which check_index.py does not recompute. The full records are kept by the task's maintainers.

environment/Dockerfile.change: the documented task-assets fetch block appended (docs/task-assets.md section 2); every earlier line unchanged

publication.note: the published form of this folder (the benchmark pull request that adds or changes the task): the payload's 77 page images and 24 CSV logs are served from the benchmark's asset dataset and staged into the agent home by environment/setup/setup.sh, at the same paths with the same bytes; nothing the agent sees changed. In the development form these files sat in environment/setup/payload/ and environment/Dockerfile had no fetch block. The numbers in `reports` were computed on the development form or on the published form. The two forms share, byte for byte, the grader's own files (tests/grade.py, tests/verify.py, tests/test.sh, tests/alelab_stop.py, tests/grader_config.json, tests/anchor.json, tests/schemas.json and tests/digest/), the procedure (tests/evaluation_basis.py), the hidden world (tests/world/), the reference (solution/) and the desk's tables (environment/setup/ref/); the vendored copy of the benchmark's shared grading kit (tests/robotics_grader/) is not shared: the published form carries the benchmark's own copy. The runs through the engine (QC's two `ale validate` runs and its largest legal submission) and the frontier-model episode (DESK) ran on the published form, on the commit described beside the reports, with the 101 files served to the image build by a local mirror of the asset list.
